title: Bechet the thinker, and the classics at the House of Meditation
summary: Zutty insists Bechet and Ladnier were deep in the Rosicrucian beliefs and spoke the same language; Bechet knew stories like the swan and no jazz records were played.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: He and Bechet were very, very deep in that.
Well I never thought Bechet was that kind, but he was a thinker though wasn't he?
Oh yes.
Somebody told me Bechet was a thinker.
Oh yes, yes indeed.
But I mean I wouldn't have thought he was serious about things like that.
Oh yes, they were well up on that stuff.
Bechet (Bashey?) too?
Bechet (Bashey) too. He and Tommy Ladnier.
They spoke the same language.
Yes.
Is that so?
That's why they could live together.
Zutty had me (unintelligible) when he came and told me that, who was it, Ladnier said that Bechet (Bashey) was the living image of Beethoven?
Yes.
The living image of Beethoven.
(LAUGHTER).
You're the dead image.
The dead image. Zutty used to tell me that's what Zutty called it, said I'm going down to The House of Meditation.
House of Meditation. And no jazz records. Only classics.
Isn't that extraordinary.

Only classics man. And old Bechet (Bashey) knew the story about a lot of those like the swan. He'd tell you how to the would swan and glide along you know. Things like that you know. How to............
